title: Fallow's Ultimate Crispy Chicken
subtitle: Hot honey · Blue cheese ranch
notes: Ingredient amounts are reconstructed home-kitchen estimates from the video transcript, not verified Fallow quantities.

groups.title: Blue cheese ranch
items: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

groups.title: Frying & finishing
items: 2–3 L canola oil, depending on pot size

steps.title: Prepare chicken · Day 1
steps.text: Cut thighs into approximately 50–70 g strips. Lightly score both sides with shallow cuts, without slicing through the meat. Mix water, salt and sriracha. Add chicken, cover and refrigerate for 24 hours at 5°C or colder.

steps.title: Make hot honey
steps.text: Combine honey, rice vinegar, sriracha, chilli flakes, Sichuan peppercorns, fennel seeds, salt and optional MSG. Warm to a gentle simmer, grate in garlic, then simmer for 2–3 minutes. Cool, refrigerate overnight, and rewarm gently before serving.

steps.title: Prepare dredges · Day 2
steps.text: Whisk all dry-dredge ingredients together. In another bowl, whisk buttermilk and cornflour until smooth.

steps.title: Build first crust
steps.text: Move a few pieces of chicken and a little clinging marinade into a separate bowl. Add a handful of dry dredge and mix vigorously to create a sticky, uneven coating. Repeat with remaining chicken. Discard unused raw marinade.

steps.title: Double dredge
steps.text: Put sticky chicken into dry dredge. Tumble and turn about 60 times to create rough clusters. Dip completely in buttermilk-cornflour wet dredge. Return to dry dredge and roll gently to coat. Tap and shake off excess flour, revealing the jagged crust. Fry promptly.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat canola oil to 185–190°C in a heavy deep pot, filled no more than one-third. Fry in small batches (typically 3–5 pieces depending on pot size), leaving pieces undisturbed initially to set the crust. Turn when set. Cook until deeply golden, approximately 5–8 minutes depending on thickness, and verify at least 75°C in the thickest part. Drain on a wire rack.

steps.title: Make blue cheese ranch
steps.text: Crumble blue cheese. Add buttermilk, Japanese mayonnaise, lemon juice, white wine vinegar, honey and onion powder. Mash gently, leaving some cheese chunks. Stir through chives and black pepper. Refrigerate until needed.

steps.title: Glaze & serve
steps.text: Dip warm chicken briefly into gently warmed hot honey, let excess drip off, sprinkle with flaky sea salt, and serve immediately with blue cheese ranch.

title: Satay Chicken — No Coconut Milk
subtitle: Peanut sauce · BBQ, air fryer or oven

groups.title: Satay sauce
items: ½ cup water, plus more to thin

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Cut chicken into even pieces. Mix the marinade and coat the chicken. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Combine sauce ingredients in a small pan. Warm gently, stirring, and thin with water to your preferred consistency.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on the BBQ for about 10–12 minutes, in the air fryer at 200°C for about 10–12 minutes, or in the oven at 220°C for about 15–18 minutes. Turn as needed. Timing depends on piece size; check chicken reaches 75°C internally.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with the warm sauce. Rice and vegetables can be prepared separately.

notes: Your no-coconut-milk version. Sauce is separate from raw-chicken marinade. Export follow-up recovered optional ½ tsp curry powder in the sauce; overnight marinating is also an option.

steps.text: Cook macaroni until just shy of fully cooked. Drain. Heat oven to 180°C.

steps.title: Make sauce

steps.title: Assemble

steps.title: Bake

title: Chicken Mince Bolognese — 1 kg Batch
subtitle: Family batch · Soy milk optional

steps.title: Soften vegetables
steps.text: Heat oil and sauté onion, carrot and optional celery for 6–8 minutes. Add garlic for 30–60 seconds.

steps.title: Brown mince
steps.text: Brown the mince in two batches, breaking up lumps. Return all mince and vegetables to the pan.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Fry tomato paste for 1–2 minutes. Add tomatoes, stock, herbs, paprika and Worcestershire. Season to taste.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer uncovered for 35–45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add optional soy milk during the last 10 minutes. Add a little water if too thick; cook longer uncovered if too thin. Ensure chicken mince is cooked through.

steps.title: Serve or portion
steps.text: Serve with separately cooked pasta, or cool promptly and portion for the freezer.

notes: Recovered 1 kg batch using one 400 g tin of tomatoes. This is a mince sauce, not a meatball mixture. Export follow-up recovered optional 1 tsp sugar; add only if needed when tasting. The saved recipe date and visible request date differ.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
subtitle: Low and slow · BBQ finish

items: ½ cup apple juice or cider vinegar

groups.title: Finish

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Mix rub ingredients. Coat pork and place on the sliced onion in the slow cooker. Add the cooking liquid.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Cook on LOW for 8–10 hours until easily pulled apart. Use tenderness rather than time alone.

steps.title: Shred
steps.text: Lift pork out, remove string and large fat pieces, then shred. Reserve and skim the cooking liquid.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Mix pork with some reserved juices and BBQ sauce to taste. If you want to divide into different flavours, divide the plain shredded pork first.

steps.title: Optional crisp
steps.text: Spread pork on a tray and crisp at 220°C for 10–15 minutes, watching closely.

notes: The BBQ base was recovered. The exact separate taco-finishing mix was not retrieved, so it has not been invented.

title: Chicken, Brie & Mushroom Risotto

steps.text: Sear chicken in a little oil, then set aside. Brown mushrooms separately.

steps.text: Soften onion in butter and oil, add garlic, then toast rice for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Add stock
steps.text: Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Return chicken and mushrooms after about 8–10 minutes. Continue adding stock until rice is tender and chicken is cooked through to 75°C.

steps.title: Finish off heat
steps.text: Take off heat. Stir in brie, a little butter, optional cheddar and spinach. Loosen with stock if needed.

title: Wholemeal Sourdough in the Cloche
subtitle: Wholemeal flour · Overnight ferment · Cloche

steps.title: Autolyse
steps.text: Mix flour and water until no dry patches remain. Cover and rest for 30–45 minutes.

steps.title: Mix dough
steps.text: Work in the active starter and salt until evenly combined.

steps.title: Strengthen
steps.text: Do four sets of stretch and folds, about 30 minutes apart.

steps.title: Bulk ferment
steps.text: Keep covered until the dough has risen about 30–50% and feels aerated. The chat estimated another 1–3 hours after folds, but temperature and dough activity determine timing.

steps.title: Shape and refrigerate
steps.text: Shape a boule and place seam-side up in a well-floured banneton or lined bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 8–16 hours.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the assembled cloche at 250°C for 45–60 minutes on a lower-middle shelf. Allow the full hour for the under-bench oven.

steps.title: Score and bake
steps.text: Turn out the cold dough onto baking paper, score briskly, and load the hot cloche. Bake covered at 250°C for 20–25 minutes, then uncovered at 220–230°C for 20–25 minutes. No added ice or water is needed in the cloche. Aim for 96–99°C internally.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack for 1–2 hours before slicing.

notes: Your recorded dough quantities, retained exactly. Fermentation time is a guide; watch the dough.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Stretch and top with your chosen toppings. Bake in a pizza oven at 450–500°C for about 60–90 seconds, turning as needed.

title: Crème Brûlée
subtitle: Cream and vanilla custard with a caramelised sugar crust
time: 35–45 min baking + cooling + at least 4 hours chilling
servings: One 600 mL cream batch; ramekin count not recovered

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat oven to 150°C. Warm cream with vanilla. Whisk egg yolks, caster sugar and salt, then gradually whisk in the warm cream. Divide among ramekins.

steps.title: Bake in a water bath
steps.text: Place ramekins in a deep baking dish and add hot water around them to form a water bath. Bake at 150°C for 35–45 minutes until the edges are set and the centres still wobble gently.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Remove ramekins from the water bath, cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

steps.title: Caramelise
steps.text: Distribute the topping sugar in thin layers over the cold custards; the retrieved guidance was about 1 tsp per ramekin. Torch until caramelised. Let the crust harden before serving.

notes: Method wording reconstructed from recovered chat instructions; complete transcripts and later corrections were not available. Ramekin count, size, cream-heating temperature and water-bath depth were not recovered.
